newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: FEATURE - Foreign influx boosts Singapore vice trade.
newsitem.headline: FEATURE - Foreign influx boosts Singapore vice trade.

text.p: It is known as the "four floors of whores", located at the tip of Orchard Road, Singapore's plush central shopping street.
The building, packed with bars staffed by hostesses, is the first stop for many in their search for a good time in a city-state with a reputation for a clean, well-ordered life free of sleaze.
After midnight on weekends, business may spill onto the sidewalks as prostitutes and a scattering of transvestites attempt to lure passers-by.
Police patrol the area to crack down on soliciting and pimping, which are illegal.
Prostitution, however, is not and there is a surprisingly wide variety on offer in Singapore, despite its somewhat puritanical reputation.
INFLUX OF FOREIGN WORKERS BOOSTS VICE TRADE

Along Orchard Road, expensive karaoke lounges, bars, pubs and fancy discotheques cater to local and foreign patrons, who include expatriate workers, here because of labour shortages in booming Singapore.
"There's nothing wrong in mixing business with a little pleasure," commented an Orchard Road bar owner.
The influx of foreigners has not only boosted a business established long ago around the bustling port, but has changed the nature of the island's sex-for-sale trade.

Chinese and Japanese businessmen frequent karaoke lounges and their hostesses. There are Irish pubs, American eateries and Country and Western bars plumped near massage parlours which mainly cater to Western businessmen.
For the blue collar construction workers and local patrons, there is Desker Road, Geylang and Keong Saik Street, where prices can be as low as S$20 (US$14) a session.
Around Desker Road, near Singapore's Little India, construction workers from the Asian subcontinent frequent back-street brothels.
SOME BROTHELS REMAIN IN OLD DOWNTOWN AREA
One of them, Rakesh, 23, said they are good places to look for friends and companions. "It gets lonely sometimes working in Singapore," he says.

Tucked away in Geylang, rows of pre-World War Two houses, some of which were brothels, have been delicately conserved as a reminder of old Singapore amid the new skyscrapers. A few are still brothels.
Tan runs one of what he said must be around 250 brothels in the area. He said an influx of Thai girls two years ago to make quick money has changed the atmosphere.
"Suddenly there appeared Thai marts, eateries and hair saloons," he said.
He told Reuters that government regulations on these premises are strict. "But that has not affected business," he added.

"Police officers come here quite often to do their checks as sometimes there are girls from Thailand, Vietnam or the Philippines who are not licensed and are here on tourist visas. There are just here looking for quick money," he said in a mixture of English and the Chinese Hokkien dialect.
Tan said these girls earned between $80-$350 (US$55-240) a night.
Establishments around Keong Saik road, near old Chinatown, are most popular with local Chinese patrons.
RED LANTERNS DEFY MODERNISATION DRIVE
While Singapore's young working adults hang out at the French-style "Opera Cafe", oddly situated among old shops and houses, tousled middle-aged men stumble out of the dimly-lit doorways.
With modernisation, this once popular red light district has made way for boutiques, hotels, advertising agencies and design companies.
But a scattering of brothels still remain -- red lanterns, though dusty with age, seem defiant and reluctant to give way to modern business.
The owner of a coffee shop nearby said although the place has changed, it is business as usual for many of the women he knows. "Some of them are very old already," he said.

Lily (not her real name) said she has been in the trade for more than six years. The petite and good-looking Chinese woman said she was in her late thirties, though she appeared much younger and was only a part-timer.
"Nobody's is in it for fun, I do it for the money, Singapore is a very expensive place to live, you know," she said in almost posh English.
Prostitutes in Singapore are licensed by means of a yellow card, which establishes identity and profession. It carries a photograph and thumbprint.
Its continued possession also requires the woman to visit a doctor every fortnight for a check-up.
But not every customer goes away pleased about the Singapore sex scene.
"The prices in Singapore are way too high, the services are pathetic and the selection can be downright embarrassing," said one Westerner.
